No—you almost certainly would **not** be able to spot the Moon at that moment.

Its altitude is about **−6.9°**, meaning it is nearly seven degrees below the geometric horizon. Even with clear skies and normal eyesight, terrain, buildings, and atmospheric extinction would block it. Civil twilight does not make objects below the horizon visible; it only describes the Sun’s position and the resulting sky brightness.

The Moon’s illumination and distance don’t change that conclusion. Unless you had an unusually elevated or unobstructed view toward the horizon and were seeing some exceptional atmospheric refraction—which is very unlikely—you would not see it.
